XDOCUMENTO.Titolo: Guide to reading EOBD fault codes

XCAPITOLO.Corpo:
Fault codes (DTC) EOBD / OBDII can be read by the car mechanic using a standardised diagnostic tester ( Scantool ). They consist of a letter followed by four digits. The first letter of the code represents the vehicle system where the fault occurred:

P- (powertrain): engine (standard EOBD codes: P0000 - P1000)

B- (body): climate control, lights, windscreen washers, seats, door locks, window locks, mirrors, airbag sensors, GPS, car radio...

C- (chassis): ABS, traction and stability control, active shock absorber control, power steering

U- (network): communication errors on the data network

  • The first number on the left indicates: if 0 or 2 (standard codes), if 1 (reserved codes)
  • the second number on the left identifies the subsystem where the fault occurred:

    1- faults in the injection system sensors
    2- faults in the injection system actuators
    3- faults in the injection system or misfires
    4- faults in the emission control system
    5- faults in the vehicle speed, A/C and power steering sensors
    6- faults in the transmission system (clutch and gearbox)
    7- transmission system faults

  • the third and last digits specifically indicate the type of fault, based on the exact European regulatory description.

  • Further information is provided in the references at the bottom of the page
